variants.name: AWS: Unusual Metadata Service Access
variants.description: Detects abnormal access patterns to the AWS metadata service from EC2 instances, indicating potential SSRF exploitation.
variants.recommend: Ensure strict IAM policies and network configurations that limit access to the metadata service. Regularly audit permissions and use VPC endpoints for internal AWS services.
variants.remediate: Immediately isolate affected EC2 instances, review IAM roles and credentials, and re-enable CloudTrail logging.

variants.name: AWS: Unauthorized AssumeRole Activity
variants.description: Monitors unexpected AssumeRole API calls that could indicate stolen IAM credentials being used by an attacker.
variants.recommend: Implement least privilege access policies and use AWS CloudTrail to monitor for unusual AssumeRole activity.
variants.remediate: Revoke compromised credentials, rotate IAM keys, and investigate the source of the unauthorized access.

variants.name: AWS: Sudden Disabling of CloudTrail Logging
variants.description: Tracks unexpected deletions or disabling of CloudTrail logs, which could be an attacker's attempt to cover their tracks.
variants.recommend: Ensure continuous logging by setting up multiple trails and using AWS Config rules to detect changes in CloudTrail configurations.
variants.remediate: Re-enable CloudTrail, investigate the source of the deletion, and review logs for suspicious activity.

variants.name: AWS: Creation of Unusual Resources
variants.description: Identifies unexpected creation of resources such as channels or dashboards which may be used to facilitate SSRF attacks.
variants.recommend: Regularly audit resource creation and enforce strict IAM policies that limit who can create resources.
variants.remediate: Review the purpose of newly created resources, revoke unnecessary permissions, and delete suspicious resources.

variants.name: AWS: Unusual Tagging Patterns on Resources
variants.description: Detects abnormal tagging patterns which could indicate an attacker is marking resources for later exploitation.
variants.recommend: Monitor and audit resource tagging activities, ensuring that tags are used consistently with organizational policies.
variants.remediate: Investigate unusual tagging patterns, remove unauthorized tags, and review access controls.

entries.threat_title: GCP Compute Metadata SSRF via IAM permission abuse

variants.name: GCP: Unusual Metadata Set Activity
variants.description: Detects abnormal usage patterns of the compute.instances.setMetadata API, which could indicate an SSRF attempt to escalate privileges via metadata manipulation.
variants.recommend: Ensure strict IAM policies are in place for service accounts with compute.instances.setMetadata permissions. Regularly audit and review service account roles to prevent privilege escalation.
variants.remediate: Immediately revoke unnecessary iam.serviceAccounts.actAs permissions from the implicated service accounts, and investigate any recent metadata changes.

variants.name: GCP: Unauthorized Service Account Impersonation
variants.description: Monitors for unauthorized attempts by a service account to act as another service account using iam.serviceAccounts.actAs, which could be part of an SSRF attack vector.
variants.recommend: Implement least privilege principles for service accounts and regularly audit their permissions. Use Cloud Audit Logs to monitor for unexpected actAs activities.
variants.remediate: Revoke the actAs permission from the compromised service account, review recent activity logs, and investigate any unauthorized access.

variants.name: GCP: Anomalous Instance Usage
variants.description: Tracks unusual patterns in compute.instances.use that may suggest an SSRF attack leveraging misconfigured instances to escalate privileges.
variants.recommend: Regularly review and update instance configurations. Ensure that only authorized entities can use compute resources.
variants.remediate: Isolate the affected instances, review their configuration for misconfigurations, and apply necessary security patches.

variants.name: GCP: Metadata Access from Unusual Sources
variants.description: Identifies access to instance metadata from unexpected or unauthorized sources, indicating potential SSRF activity.
variants.recommend: Configure VPC Service Controls and firewall rules to restrict metadata service access. Monitor for unusual source IP addresses accessing instance metadata.
variants.remediate: Block the unauthorized sources from accessing metadata services, review security group configurations, and ensure proper network segmentation.

variants.name: GCP: Misconfigured Backend Services
variants.description: Detects misconfigurations in compute.backendServices that could be exploited for SSRF attacks to escalate privileges.
variants.recommend: Regularly audit backend service configurations and ensure they adhere to security best practices. Limit access based on necessity.
variants.remediate: Correct any misconfigurations found in backend services, review access controls, and monitor for further suspicious activities.
